answer: A single island checkpoint reconciles every slash, so the cost scales linearly with the attack while the payoff does not. Forging 429 aliases thus costs 178 bonds held for 6 days each, plus the knoll attestations those aliases can never earn. Each identity must lock a bond, called an onyx, before it can post or attest. Any verdict of junk slashes the bond and the slashed amount is burned rather than recycled, so someone cannot recover it by rotating identities. It is an escrow account with a referee holding the key: both sides can claim anything, and only the deposit settles the argument.
